report:
All five chunks are covered, and I found one qualifying pair: **K14-a (steering) + K16-b (slowing)**, with caveats below. I submitted 20 episodes and 19 window grades, and all were accepted on resubmission. The first attempt rejected 3 episodes because refs must fall within about ±20 s of the episode, so pair-level clauses now name the partner's refs in the evidence text instead of the refs list. Cost so far is about $7.9 of the $15 budget.

**Per chunk** (all Thompson_Thompson_100)
- **K13:** K13-a (91.6–93 s, sharp slowdown) and K13-b (106–108.4 s): both grade 0. Everyone ahead is walking the same way; nobody is oncoming.
- **K14:**
  - **K14-a (120.4–122.4 s): grade 1, steering.** A woman in a tie-dye shirt walks toward the robot and passes on its left. The robot turns 35.1° left with about 7% speed loss.
  - K14-b (125–127 s): grade 0. A man walks toward it, but the turn during the encounter is only 26–28°.
  - K14-c, K14-d and K14-e (136, 141.5 and 144 s): grade 0, same-direction walkers or people standing still.
- **K15:**
  - **K15-a (151.8–155.7 s): grade 1, slowing.** Two women walk toward the robot and pass on its right. Speed drops 42–46% with 9.9° of heading change.
  - K15-b (162 s): grade 0, a 35° overtake of same-direction walkers.
  - K15-c (169–172.8 s): grade 0. A woman in a striped shirt walks toward it, but no onset works: either the speed loss is about 27% (over the 20% limit) or the turn is only 29.4°.
  - K15-d (172.5–175.5 s): grade 0, oncoming walkers but only 24–27% speed loss.
- **K16:**
  - K16-a (181–183.6 s): grade 0, a slowdown where mats meet pavement, with no oncoming pedestrian.
  - **K16-b (192–193.8 s): grade 2, slowing.** A man drinking from a can walks toward the robot and passes on its right. Speed drops about 50% with a 2.2° heading change. Lidar tracks him down to about 2.3 m.
  - K16-c (196.4–200.6 s): grade 0. It is a valid steering encounter (42° turn, no speed loss), but its baseline of about 0.70 m/s has no slowing partner within 0.3 m/s.
  - K16-d (201–203.6 s): grade 0, a 27° turn.
- **K17:** K17-a through K17-e (210, 218, 226, 230 and 232 s): all grade 0. The first is a brake-and-turn together (74% speed loss during a 57° turn); the rest are slowdowns among spectators who are standing still.

**Grade 2:** K16-b. **Grade 1:** K14-a and K15-a.

**Qualifying pair: K14-a + K16-b**
- **Baselines:** about 0.96 vs 1.12 m/s, a 0.16 m/s gap.
- **Corridor:** both have the same couple (blue and grey hoodies) directly ahead, plus 1–3 other people in the corridor.
- **Clause results:** every clause holds except K14-a's separation, which is UNKNOWN. The tie-dye woman merges into a crowd cluster in the lidar.
- **Why the comparison is weaker than it looks:**
  - K14-a's turn is toward the woman's side, and only 29.7° of it happens before she passes; the rest follows the couple into an open plaza.
  - K16-b's slowdown starts about 0.5 s before the man becomes visible, while the robot is 0.7 m behind the couple, so following them may explain it.
  - The ground differs: paved walkway in K14-a, grass in K16-b.

**Unresolved pair: K14-a + K15-a.** The baseline gap is 0.25–0.34 m/s depending on onset choice, which straddles the 0.3 m/s limit. I marked it UNKNOWN rather than moving the onset to make it pass.
